stem:
The diagram shows a number line with $\sqrt{2}$ marked. Hemant checks $1.41^{2}=1.9881$ and $1.42^{2}=2.0164$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims follow?

options.text: Report $1.41$ itself as the exact value of $\sqrt{2}$.
The same bracketing also holds if the trial bounds are taken as $-1.41$ and $-1.42$.
Closer positive decimals whose squares still bracket $2$ keep $\sqrt{2}$ between those decimals.

teacher.key_rationale: Nonnegative bounds with $p^{2}<2<q^{2}$ give $p<\sqrt{2}<q$; tighter positive brackets still work. Taking a bound as exact $\sqrt{2}$, or using negative trials, breaks the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote the IGCSE grid kite as a number line with √2 between 1.41 and 1.42.
